title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 126
paragraphs: Then in the next generation after this, Cleisthenes the tyrant of Sicyon raised the family still higher, so that it became much more famous among the Greeks than before. Cleisthenes son of Aristonymus, son of Myron, son of Andreas, had a daughter named Agariste, and he made it his purpose to find the best man in Greece and marry her to him. So when the Olympic games were being held and Cleisthenes won them with a four-horse chariot, he had it proclaimed that any Greek who considered himself worthy to be Cleisthenes's son-in-law should come to Sicyon by the sixtieth day, or sooner if he wished, for Cleisthenes meant to conclude the marriage within a year, counting from that sixtieth day. All those Greeks who took pride either in themselves or in their high birth came as suitors, and for them Cleisthenes had built a running-track and a wrestling-ground kept expressly for their use.
